items.title: DIGITAL IDENTITY
items.headline: Verify and manage your Haitian Digital Identity
items.intro: The Unique Identification Number (NINU) is the official identifier for every Haitian citizen, issued by the National Identification Office (ONI). Two official platforms allow you to manage your identity online.
steps: Verify your NINU (10 digits) via DELIDOC ONI — real-time status tracking
Lost or stolen card? Submit your complaint on the DELIDOC ONI portal
Entering Haiti? Complete the iKat form (Digital Arrival Form) before your arrival
For a passport application, access DELIDOC Passport — new application or file tracking
Need help? Contact ONI at +509 2813-1111 or email: support@oni.gouv.ht

items.title: PASSPORTS
items.headline: Apply for or renew your Haitian passport from abroad
items.intro: The Haitian passport is issued by the Directorate of Immigration and Emigration. From abroad, initiate and track your application online via DELIDOC Passport.
steps: Access DELIDOC Passport (delidoc.gouv.ht/DemandePasseport)
Create an account or log in with your NINU
Fill out the application form and upload your documents
Pay consular fees online and submit your file
Track your file's progress using your DELIDOC reference number

items.title: NATIONAL ARCHIVES
items.headline: Obtain your certified civil status documents
items.intro: The National Archives of Haiti preserve and issue civil status record extracts. As a diaspora member, you can request your documents remotely.
steps: Identify the type of document needed (birth, marriage, death)
Send your request to archives@mhave.gouv.ht with a copy of your ID
Attach proof of relationship with the person concerned
Pay the processing fees (variable depending on the document)
Receive your certified document within 10–15 business days

items.title: LEGALIZATION
items.headline: Have your official Haitian documents legalized or apostilled
items.intro: Legalization and apostille allow your Haitian documents to be recognized in a foreign country. MHAVE coordinates these procedures with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
steps: Gather the original documents (notarized acts, diplomas, civil records)
First legalize with the Haitian Ministry of Justice
Submit to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for the apostille
If you are abroad, contact the competent Haitian consulate
Timeframe: 5 to 10 business days depending on the document type

sections.label: Mission & Vision
sections.content: MHAVE is the official interface between the Haitian government and the 4 million diaspora members spread across more than 35 countries.
items: Strengthen ties between Haiti and its diaspora
Facilitate access to government services from abroad
Protect the rights of Haitians living abroad
Promote Haitian cultural identity around the world
